gap.title: The Sketch Law: low-dose LoRA-DPO as a random sketch of one data-determined function, and the rank and dose at which seed-invariance breaks
gap.central_question: Is the function learned by standard-recipe LoRA-DPO (lr 5e-6, 1 epoch, PEFT default init B=0 / A kaiming, TRL trainer with peft_config) a seed-independent functional of (base, data, program) that each unseeded lora_A merely sketches -- dW = B*A0 ~ -sum_t lr_t * adam(G_t A0^T) A0, a Johnson-Lindenstrauss estimator of ONE data-determined gradient direction in function space, orthogonal in weight space by construction -- so that (i) cross-run weight cosines carry no mechanistic information unless A0 is shared, (ii) function space is the only valid space for 'same solution' claims, and (iii) the invariance breaks predictably when rank falls below the preference gradient's effective rank k_eff, or when the trajectory leaves the first-order regime (reward-margin saturation at high dose, F5c), with A-displacement explicitly ruled out as the regime variable because Probe 2 shows lora_A frozen even at 40x lr and 3 epochs?
gap.hypothesis: At the paper recipe A stays within ~2% of its unseeded kaiming init (sum-of-lr bound: sum lr ~1.6e-4 vs element scale ~0.009), and data order is seeded identically (SeedableRandomSampler from seed 42 applied AFTER the PEFT wrap), so each seed's adapter is an independent random sketch of the SAME data-determined gradient G. Falsifiable consequences: (a) seeded twins (seed set before get_peft_model) share lora_A bitwise and reach per-layer dW cosine > 0.9, the residual being kernel nondeterminism; (b) different-seed adapters have weight cosine ~1/sqrt(r*fan_in) ~ 0.004 yet per-token logit-delta cosine > 0.8 and disattenuated per-task profile r >= 0.9 (the reliability ceiling F5b already shows for three 4090 retrains), on both raw and typing-forgiven metrics, and across the 4090 and 5080 stacks; (c) freezing A reproduces gain and profile; (d) the rank-32 concatenation average of two orthogonal adapters preserves the gain although ||dW||_F falls by 1/sqrt(2) (sketch averaging is variance reduction, not basin averaging, refuting magnitude primacy in this regime); (e) between-seed profile agreement declines monotonically with rank below k_eff (working form r_seed ~ 1/(1 + k_eff/r); the r=16 ceiling implies k_eff <~ 2); (f) left (output-side) top-k singular subspaces of dW are shared across seeds while right (input-side) subspaces sit at chance, reconciling Hu et al. Sec. 7.2 with F3; (g) a second adapter at the positive-control recipe (lr 2e-4 x 3 epochs, margins ~11) does NOT reproduce the first's per-task profile (disattenuated r < 0.8), whereas early-stopped high-lr runs (train accuracy < 0.9 at stop) agree with each other and with the low-lr consensus -- predictive multiplicity is a signature of margin saturation, not of step size or of A moving; (h) any TRL-based LoRA run that reports a seed has an init the seed never reached, detectable in released adapters.

What exists: lazy-A theory ('The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics'), frozen/random-A results ('Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models', 'VeRA', 'HydraLoRA'), random-subspace intrinsic dimension ('Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning'), benign-landscape theory ('LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima', 'LoRA Training Provably Converges to a Low-Rank Global Minimum or It Fails Loudly'), thin-shell regularity ('Model Stock'), location consistency for full-FT RL ('Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models', 'The Path Not Taken') -- all for SFT/vision/full-FT, none measuring function-space agreement of seed-orthogonal LoRA-DPO adapters or its breakdown with rank or dose. Nobody has (a) a second seed in the rich regime to show multiplicity returning, (b) the averaging test, (c) function-space cosine next to weight-space orthogonality, (d) the Hu 7.2 left/right resolution, (e) a frozen-A arm under DPO, or (f) an audit of released TRL adapters. The project's head start is unique: Probe 1 already answered the map's open profile question at zero compute (disattenuated r 1.06/1.08/1.06; 1.12/1.13/1.11 typing-forgiven), Probe 2 measured A-drift and matched the predicted 0.0039 against the measured 0.0042, and both boundary cases are banked (F5: original adapter r = -0.10, reliability 0.21/0.52; F5c: poscontrol r 0.43-0.56, SD 33pp vs 16pp, margins 11 vs 0.78).
predictions: Zero-compute sketch signature: a random-projection simulation of all 224 module shapes reproduces the recorded per-layer dW cosine 0.0042 +/- 0.0044 ONLY when B_i = G*A0_i^T with a shared G (independent random B gives mean ~0; the recorded mean is ~14 SE above zero), and splits by module: q/k/v/o/gate/up (fan_in 4096) ~0.0039 vs down_proj (fan_in 14336) ~0.0021 under 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) (1.9x smaller) versus ~3.5x smaller under r/d_in -- the simulation plus the per-module compare_adapters.py output adjudicates the scaling. Hu-style top-k subspace similarity phi(k=1..4) on the RIGHT side is at chance (< 0.05). REFUTED if independent-B simulation already yields the positive mean, if down_proj cosines are not smaller, or if real retrains share right-side top directions (restores Hu Sec. 7.2 and kills the pure lazy-A account).

Seeded twins (same seed set before get_peft_model): lora_A 224/224 bitwise identical (poscontrol/init_vs_training.py); per-layer dW cosine >= 0.9; profile r at the reliability ceiling. REFUTED if dW cosine < 0.5 -- kernel nondeterminism alone would then decorrelate weights (Summers-Dinneen regime), not the random A0.

Different-seed pair (s1, s2; lr 5e-6 x 1 epoch; same 5080 session): weight-space dW cosine 0.004 +/- 0.005 but per-position logit-delta cosine on the 31 ruler prompts >= 0.8 (>= 0.5 minimum), disattenuated per-task profile r >= 0.9 on raw AND aggregate_if_typing_imported, both arms >= +7pp vs the interleaved null and within 3pp of each other; cross-stack class membership: raw r >= 0.8 with the 4090 retrain consensus (the same six tasks ace_oss_11023/17851/4327/24748/23069/23132 gain >= +25pp, ace_oss_3243 loses >= 10pp, typing NameErrors ~2 per 155). REFUTED if logit-delta cosine < 0.3 while profiles still agree (identity would then not be first-order), if profile r < 0.7 (F5b does not transfer to this stack), or if cross-stack r < 0.5 (function stack-dependent; F1 must be re-read as a stack effect rather than a fault).

Frozen-A arm (lora_A.requires_grad=False, same seed as a trained-A twin): aggregate within the 15-replicate MDE (~4pp) of the trained-A twin; disattenuated typing-forgiven profile r >= 0.9; compare_adapters.py cosine ~1 (shared A0). REFUTED if frozen-A loses >= 5pp or r < 0.7 (A's small drift carries function).

Rank-32 concatenation average of the two different-seed adapters ([A1;A2], [B1/2, B2/2]): ||dW||_F ~ 0.71x a parent, yet aggregate gain within +/-2pp of the parents' mean (e.g., parents +9pp, average >= +7pp) and profile r with each parent >= 0.9. REFUTED (magnitude primacy / random-subspace energy view, Model Stock center-approximation) if the average's gain <= 0.75x the parents' or recovers only after sqrt(2) rescaling.

Rank sweep at alpha/r = 2, lr = 5e-6*sqrt(16/r), two seeds per rank: between-seed disattenuated profile r falls monotonically with rank; with the r=16 ceiling implying k_eff <= ~2, predict r=4 in 0.7-0.9 and r=1 in 0.35-0.7. Weight-space corollary on the same adapters: principal angles between col(B_seed1) and col(B_seed2) (left singular subspaces of dW) are small for the shared k_eff directions while row spaces (span of A0) are orthogonal; output-side top-4 subspace similarity exceeds input-side similarity by >= 5x per module, and the weight-space k_eff estimate agrees with the behavioral one within a factor of 2. REFUTED if r=1 twins still agree >= 0.9 on the typing-forgiven profile (a global attractor, not a sketch), if col(B) subspaces are also mutually orthogonal, or if right-side similarity is high (A aligned to data, contradicting Probe 2). If both sides are at chance (~r/d), G's effective rank exceeds r -- also informative.

Regime boundary: a second unseeded lr 2e-4 x 3-epoch adapter vs the existing dpo_adapter_poscontrol, same session: mean gain +11 +/- 4pp but disattenuated per-task r <= 0.7 (split-half reliabilities >= 0.85), per-task delta SD ~30pp, opposite sign on >= 5 tasks that swing more than 30pp, typing fails ~0.1/row. Early-stopped high-lr arms (lr 2e-4, --max-steps 17, two seeds; train accuracy < 0.9, margins < 2 at stop) agree with each other at the ceiling AND correlate >= 0.8 (disattenuated) with the low-lr consensus, with larger per-task SD. REFUTED if the two poscontrol seeds agree >= 0.9 (a deterministic second lr-indexed attractor; multiplicity absent in both regimes), if early-stopped seeds disagree with each other (step size, not saturation, breaks invariance), or if they agree with each other but not with the low-lr profile (lr selects a different deterministic function).

Optional dose-response: an lr 2e-5 x 1-epoch adapter has disattenuated r with the low-lr consensus between 0.8 and 0.95 and per-task SD between 17 and 33pp, i.e. profile agreement declines monotonically with sum(lr). Zero-compute companion: the three retrain logs' loss/margin trajectories coincide to 2-3 decimals across seeds while training_poscontrol.log saturates (accuracy 1.0 from epoch ~1.7, margins 10-11); the saturation step is the predicted onset of seed-dependence, testable by checkpoint-level fingerprints.
A displacement at the original recipe ||A_T - A_0||_F / ||A_0||_F < 0.02 in all 224 layers (measurable only with seeded A0). REFUTED if > 0.10 in any attention layer.

gap.theoretical_payoff: Establishes (or refutes) that conventional-learning-rate LoRA post-training is sketch-and-readout / random-feature regression on a frozen unseeded projection: the map (data, program) -> FUNCTION is deterministic while (data, program) -> WEIGHTS is a random orthogonal family. Consequences: (i) seed-invariance of the learned function is guaranteed once r exceeds k_eff, independent of init, so the behavioral agreement-vs-rank curve is an estimator of the intrinsic rank of the preference signal -- unifying LoRA Without Regret's ~1 bit/episode capacity argument, Aghajanyan's intrinsic dimension, Hu et al.'s shared top directions (a left-side / A-training artifact) and Mukherjee/Zhu's location-consistent full-FT RL updates (the consistent object is G, which LoRA sketches) under one mechanism; (ii) weight-space similarity of adapters is the wrong instrument (cos ~ 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) is a tautology) and function space the right one, so Nikolich et al.'s cross-objective cosines need a seed floor and Model Stock's thin shell is reached at its 90-degree extreme; (iii) predictive multiplicity (Marx; McCoy; D'Amour; Jordan) is NOT a universal property of fine-tuning but a signature of leaving the first-order regime (reward-margin saturation), with A-displacement ruled out -- the first regime boundary for underspecification in post-training; (iv) soups of orthogonal adapters are variance reduction, not basin averaging, and magnitude primacy fails in this regime; (v) every TRL-based LoRA-DPO/SFT/GRPO paper that reports seeds has an init the seed never reached -- a one-line upstreamable fix, and an adapter reproducible as (seed, B) at half the size (VeRA-like); (vi) reproducibility and attestation of LoRA post-training must be certified in function space, supplying the calibrated, replica-free, seed-free functional acceptance test that the silent-corruption and ZK-attestation literatures lack (Gap 4 builds on it). Matters to LoRA/PEFT theorists, model-merging work, RL-with-LoRA practitioners, anyone reporting single-seed or 'seed variance' of TRL LoRA runs, and training-integrity researchers.
risks: Stack transfer: the 4090 retrains (torch 2.6/cu124, py3.11) vs this RTX 5080 (torch 2.11/cu128, py3.12, bnb 0.50.1); the different-seed pair is itself a replication and may fail for stack reasons unrelated to the theory -- the within-session frozen-vs-trained and twin contrasts are primary, the cross-stack comparison secondary; a local r=16 twin pair removes the confound.

Frozen-A and seeding require wrapping the model yourself before DPOTrainer; trl 0.12.2 must accept a pre-wrapped PeftModel (it checks is_peft_model) and prepare_model_for_kbit_training is currently called twice -- validate on a --max-steps 1 smoke run first.

Adam's per-coordinate normalization and DPO's nonlinearity in B distort the linear sketch scaling; the exact 1/(1+k/r) form may fail while the monotone-in-rank ordering survives -- preregister the qualitative ordering as primary. The sketch model also predicts seed noise ~1/sqrt(r*m) with m ~224 (~2% at r=16, ~7% at r=1), below the instrument's reliability floor, so the rank sweep may not discriminate; the averaging test and the saturation boundary are the discriminating experiments, and the averaging test assumes first-order linearity at ||dW||_F ~0.02/layer.

n=15 replicates per arm gives an aggregate MDE of ~4pp and per-task profiles at 75 draws/task (rep3-level split-half ~0.69), so disattenuated correlations carry CIs of roughly +/-0.2; bootstrap CIs are mandatory; low-rank arms with smaller gains may be underpowered (mitigated by lr ~ 1/sqrt(r) compensation and pooling seeds); 20 rounds (+80 min) if a session allows.

Profile agreement may be dominated by the shared typing-import behavior (F2 NEW, 51-58% of the gain); all correlations must be reported on aggregate_if_typing_imported as well (Probe 1 shows identity holds there too), and if Gap 2's typing-ablated corpus is available the rank sweep should be repeated on it.
peft's alpha/r scaling confounds rank with effective lr; hold alpha/r = 2 (not the default alpha=32).

GGUF export of a rank-32 merged adapter via the Ollama ADAPTER path is untested; export_adapter.py's acceptance checks must pass before the arm is scored, and the served-Q4 vs PEFT-fp16 discrepancy (heldin_history not_the_served_artifact) adds instrument noise to the function-space vs behavior comparison; a norm-matched random-B null arm may degrade generation, so include a 0.5x-scaled variant.

Kernel nondeterminism on the 5080 (no determinism flags set) may leave seeded twins with dW cosine well below 1; that residual is itself the measured kernel term of the variance decomposition, but if large it weakens the 'A0 is the only unseeded draw' story.

TDR is unmitigated on this machine (no admin, TdrDelay unset), so every training run carries the F4 risk; a silently corrupted run would itself be an out-of-class adapter and could be misread as theory failure -- the step-1 liveness assert and Adam-bound gate are partial detectors; re-run once before concluding.

The lab PC wipes on logoff; adapters (168 MB each) are gitignored, so seeds + lora_B (+ 84 MB GGUF) must be pushed every session or the weight-space half is lost again (as happened with the 4090 adapters). Session A is ~2.9 h of a 4-h window; drop to 12 rounds rather than skip the push.

evidence: REFUTES CORE MECHANISM (the 'one data-determined direction' half): Zhang, Liu & Chen, 'LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning LLMs, Provably and Efficiently' (ICML 2025 oral) PROVES that under gradient descent LoRA adapters align with specific singular subspaces of the one-step full fine-tuning gradient. The gap's dW ~ -sum_t lr_t adam(G_t A0^T) A0 'sketch of ONE data-determined G' is this theorem restated for a random rather than gradient-chosen A0. https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01235

REFUTES 'function is a deterministic functional of (base,data,program) while weights are random': this is the kernel/lazy-regime theorem. Malladi, Wettig, Yu, Chen & Arora, 'A Kernel-Based View of Language Model Fine-Tuning' (ICML 2023) shows prompt-based LM fine-tuning often induces kernel dynamics and uses this to justify why PEFT works — in the kernel regime GD returns the min-RKHS-norm solution, a deterministic functional of (kernel, data), independent of which parameterization carries it. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05643

SAME, updated and LoRA-specific: 'Linearization Explains Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models' (Feb 2026) shows fine-tuning dynamics under a proximity-to-pretrained bias become equivalent to learning with the positive-definite NTK, quantifies how close linearized and full fine-tuning are as a function of regularization strength, and validates empirically on LoRA for LLMs. This is the gap's 'first-order regime' claim, already published with the regime-quality analysis. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08239

REFUTES 'A is a frozen random projection that can be frozen with no loss, and B carries the function': Zhu et al., 'Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models' (2024) characterizes A as a feature extractor and B as the output map, argues and shows a random untrained A performs nearly as well as a fine-tuned one, and gives an information-theoretic generalization bound that IMPROVES when only B is trained (RoBERTa, BART-Large, LLaMA-2, ViTs). The gap's prediction (c) frozen-A arm and prediction (f) left-vs-right subspace asymmetry are corollaries of this plus lazy-A. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16842

REFUTES 'seed-invariance of the function' + 'adapter reproducible as (seed, B)' + 'rank saturation estimates k_eff': Hazan, Zhang, Hartl & Levin, 'A Little Rank Goes a Long Way: Random Scaffolds with LoRA Adapters Are All You Need' (LottaLoRA, Apr 2026) states verbatim that (2) 'the frozen backbone is preferable but interchangeable — any random initialization works equally well, provided it remains fixed throughout training' and (3) 'the minimum LoRA rank at which performance saturates estimates the intrinsic dimensionality of the task', and proposes distributing 'models as adapters plus seed'. Three of the gap's headline payoffs, published four months ago. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08749

REFUTES the rank/k_eff law as new: Li, Farkhoor, Liu & Yosinski, 'Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes' (ICLR 2018) trains in randomly oriented low-dimensional subspaces, increases the dimension, and defines intrinsic dimension as where solutions first appear — the identical 'random sketch works once its rank exceeds the task's effective rank' phenomenon, in the identical random-projection instrument. https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.08838

REFUTES the k_eff <~ 2 prediction as already-theorized AND puts the rank sweep at risk of the gap's own REFUTED condition: 'Rethinking the Rank Threshold for LoRA Fine-Tuning' (May 2026) reduces the prior NTK-regime LoRA rank prescription (r(r+1)/2 > KN, i.e. r >= 12, from 'LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima') to r = 1 for BINARY classification, showing the PL inequality removes the rank threshold entirely under cross-entropy and that Rademacher bounds predict rank-one variance optimality exactly when the bias term saturates (binary, not multi-class). DPO is a binary Bradley-Terry loss. Existing theory therefore predicts r=1 twins may agree at ceiling — which the gap preregisters as REFUTING prediction 6 ('a global attractor, not a sketch'). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03724

REFUTES prediction (d), 'averaging two orthogonal adapters is variance reduction, not basin averaging': Wang, Gittens & Mahoney, 'Sketched Ridge Regression: Optimization Perspective, Statistical Perspective, and Model Averaging' (JMLR/ICML) establishes that averaging independently sketched solutions 'greatly decreases the gap between the risks of the true and sketched solutions' — the classical statement that averaging independent random sketches of one target is variance reduction. https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.04837

SAME, in the random-feature form that matches [A1;A2],[B1/2,B2/2] exactly: 'No Free Lunch From Random Feature Ensembles: Scaling Laws and Near-Optimality Conditions' (Dec 2024) proves via deterministic equivalents that in the overparameterized regime the test error of K independently trained random-feature models depends, to leading order, on ensemble size and model size ONLY through the total feature count — i.e. rank-32 concatenation of two rank-16 sketches behaves like one rank-32 sketch, with no norm-rescaling correction. https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05418

REFUTES 'the function converges to a seed-free limit once the sketch is wide enough' as new: Rudi & Rosasco, 'Generalization Properties of Learning with Random Features' (NeurIPS 2017) shows O(sqrt(n) log n) random features suffice for optimal O(1/sqrt(n)) rates — the canonical 'random draw, deterministic function' result. Reinforced by the deterministic-equivalent literature for random-feature regression ('Dimension-free deterministic equivalents and scaling laws for random feature regression', https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15699). https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.04474

REFUTES claim (iii) 'multiplicity is a signature of leaving the first-order regime' as new: Woodworth, Gunasekar, Lee, Moroshko, Savarese, Golan, Soudry & Srebro, 'Kernel and Rich Regimes in Overparametrized Models' (COLT 2020) shows the scale of initialization controls the transition between the kernel/lazy regime (GD finds the deterministic minimum-RKHS-norm solution) and the rich/active regime (initialization-dependent implicit bias), with a complete analysis of the transition. The gap's 'saturation breaks seed-invariance' IS the lazy->rich transition renamed; Chizat, Oyallon & Bach, 'On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07956) is the companion. https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09277

REFUTES 'weight-space cosine is the wrong instrument, function space is the right one' as a new methodological claim: Ding, Denain & Steinhardt, 'Grounding Representation Similarity with Statistical Testing' (NeurIPS 2021) shows CCA/CKA-style weight- and representation-space measures disagree on the basic question of whether networks differing only in random init are similar, and argues for functional-behavior grounding as the arbiter. https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01661

SAME argument, 2026, in exactly the gap's language: Schiffman, 'Transformers converge to invariant algorithmic cores' (Feb 2026) opens 'Training selects for behavior, not circuitry: many weight configurations can implement the same function... targeting invariants rather than parameterizations', and empirically shows Markov-chain transformers 'embed three-dimensional cores in NEARLY ORTHOGONAL SUBSPACES yet recover identical transition spectra' across independently trained models — orthogonal weights, one function, already demonstrated. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22600

REFUTES 'cross-run LoRA weight cosine ~ chance is unmeasured / unrecognized': 'Efficient Modular Learning through Naive LoRA Summation: Leveraging Orthogonality in High-Dimensional Models' (Aug 2025) explicitly hypothesizes and measures that independently trained LoRA deltas are approximately orthogonal in high dimension and correlates RMS cosine with merge interference; 'Rethinking Inter-LoRA Orthogonality in Adapter Merging' (Sep 2025) finds enforced orthogonality does NOT deliver the disentanglement prior work attributed to it, 'prompting a re-examination of its role'. The 'orthogonality is a high-dimensional tautology, not mechanism' point is already in the LoRA-merging literature. https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11985 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03262

PARTIALLY REFUTES the weight-space-geometry novelty and confirms one narrow surviving contribution: Nikolich et al., 'Weight-Space Geometry of Offline Reasoning Training' (Jun 2026) trains SFT/RFT/DFT/RIFT/Offline-GRPO/DPO with attention-only LoRA on identical rollouts and analyzes deltas via cosine similarity, principal-angle subspace analysis, linear mode connectivity AND CKA, reporting SFT/RFT/RIFT near-colinear (cos >= 0.97, top-1 principal angle ~7 deg) while 'DPO sits in a near-orthogonal subspace' and 'collapses late-layer CKA to ~0.46'. The instrument the gap proposes already exists and has been run on DPO; what it lacks is a same-recipe different-seed null against which 'near-orthogonal' could be read as chance. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23740

REFUTES 'weight-space location consistency across runs is unknown for RL post-training': 'The Path Not Taken: RLVR Provably Learns Off the Principals' (Nov 2025) reports that for a fixed pretrained model, updates 'consistently localize to preferred parameter regions, highly consistent across runs and largely invariant to datasets and RL recipes', explained by a Three-Gate Theory (KL anchor, model geometry, precision). The 'consistent object is G, determined by (base, data)' claim is established for full-FT RL. Companion: 'Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11711), which finds 5-30% subnetwork sparsity across 7 RL algorithms including DPO and 10 LLMs. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08567

ADJACENT PRIOR ART ON THE MEASUREMENT (closest existing instrument, and it reports the OPPOSITE default): Bui, Savova & Wang, 'Assessing the Macro and Micro Effects of Random Seeds on Fine-Tuning Large Language Models' (IJCNLP 2025) introduces a per-instance 'consistency' metric alongside macro accuracy/F1 on GLUE/SuperGLUE and finds 'significant variance at both macro and micro levels'. The macro/micro split the gap frames as new already has a name and a paper; the gap's F5b (micro agreement at the reliability ceiling) contradicts its finding rather than being unmeasured territory. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07329

ADJACENT PRIOR ART ON THE MULTIPLICITY DEFAULT: Summers & Dinneen, 'Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization' (ICML 2021) isolates sources of nondeterminism and finds 'all sources of nondeterminism have similar effects on measures of model diversity', with 'even one-bit changes in initial parameters' producing models that converge to vastly different values, attributing this to end-to-end training instability. This is the standing empirical generalization the gap contests — and it means the gap's twin-vs-seed2 contrast is a test of a known instability claim in a new (low-dose, lazy) regime rather than a new phenomenon.

SURVIVING-CONTRIBUTION CHECK — the (seed, B) artifact idea is ALSO taken: 'Kilobyte Models: Neural Networks as a Seed and a Quantized Latent' (Aug 2026) makes the deployable artifact 'a seed together with a quantized latent' because 'the basis and initialization center are reproducible from an integer seed'. Combined with LottaLoRA's 'adapters plus seed', payoff (v)'s VeRA-like half-size artifact is not open. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00860

REFUTED AS A MECHANISM, NOT AS AN EXPERIMENT. Every load-bearing theoretical element of "The Sketch Law" already exists in a neighbouring field, and a theory reviewer will say "that is the kernel regime": (a) "dW sketches ONE data-determined gradient" = LoRA-One's theorem (2502.01235); (b) "function is a deterministic functional of (base, data, program) while weights are a random family" = the kernel/lazy-regime min-norm result, now stated for LLM LoRA in 2602.08239 and Malladi et al. 2210.05643; (c) "A is a frozen random projection, B carries the function, left subspaces shared / right at chance" = Zhu et al.'s asymmetry result (2402.16842) plus lazy-A; (d) "invariance holds once r exceeds k_eff" = intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes (1804.08838) and the NTK LoRA rank threshold, already sharpened to r=1 for binary losses (2605.03724) — DPO is a binary loss; (e) "averaging orthogonal adapters is variance reduction, not basin averaging" = sketched-ridge model averaging (1702.04837) and random-feature ensemble deterministic equivalents (2412.05418), which predict the rank-32 concatenation behaves as one rank-32 sketch with no sqrt(2) correction; (f) "cross-seed weight cosine ~ 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) is a tautology" = concentration of measure, already noted empirically for independently trained LoRAs (2508.11985, 2510.03262); (g) "multiplicity returns when you leave the first-order regime" = the lazy->rich transition (2002.09277, 1812.07956); (h) "adapter = seed + B" = LottaLoRA (2604.08749) and Kilobyte Models (2608.00860). LottaLoRA alone independently states three of the gap's headline payoffs.

THE NARROWER SUB-QUESTIONS THAT REMAIN GENUINELY OPEN, in descending order of what a reviewer would call new:

1. THE DOSE-RESPONSE LOCATION (best surviving claim). Theory says a lazy->rich boundary exists; nothing says WHERE it is for preference optimization, what marks it, or that it is visible in per-item behaviour. Zero papers were found measuring cross-seed item-level agreement as a function of training dose for DPO. The specific, non-derivable claims are: the marker is reward-margin saturation rather than step size or A-displacement (Probe 2 rules out A movement); and early-stopped high-lr runs rejoin the low-lr consensus. Predictions (g) and the lr 2e-5 midpoint (8) carry this. Reframe the paper around this boundary, not around the sketch.

2. THE EMPIRICAL CONTRADICTION OF THE STANDING DEFAULT. Summers & Dinneen (all nondeterminism sources produce large diversity; one bit suffices) and Bui et al. 2503.07329 (significant micro-level seed variance on GLUE) are the field's default. Showing a regime where reliability-corrected per-item agreement sits at the instrument ceiling contradicts that default in a generative, execution-verified setting. That is a real result even though the theory predicts it — "known in principle, believed false in practice" is publishable; "known in principle" alone is not.

3. THE SEED-VARIANCE FLOOR AS A CORRECTION TO A 2026 PAPER. Nikolich et al. (2606.23740) report "DPO sits in a near-orthogonal subspace" from LoRA delta cosines with no same-recipe different-seed null; 2508.11985 correlates RMS cosine with merge interference on the same unfloored instrument. Supplying the floor (F3's 0.0042 against 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) = 0.0039, with the per-module down_proj split) shows their DPO signal may be at chance. Cheap, concrete, and it corrects live literature — but it is a one-figure correction, not a paper.

4. THE TRL SEEDING-ORDER DEFECT AND THE RELEASED-ADAPTER AUDIT (predictions h and 10). No adjacent field owns this; nothing was found auditing library seed ordering or bitwise lora_A identity in released adapters. It is engineering, not theory, and it is self-undercutting in this framing: if the function is seed-invariant, an unseeded init is nearly harmless. Publish it as an upstream patch plus a short reproducibility note, not as a theoretical payoff.

gap.title: Compliance before competence: offline DPO amplifies an environment-conditional verifier regularity from a minority of contrast pairs into the majority of a measured gain, and construct-valid gain is what survives a verifier-environment swap
gap.central_question: When the oracle's error is a deterministic function of the verification environment rather than a stochastic flip -- the pinned Python 3.11 verifier raises NameError on un-imported typing annotations that Python >= 3.14 accepts, and the AceCode prompts carry annotated signatures -- and the same verifier both labels the preference pairs and scores the benchmark, does offline DPO learn that instrument component first, faster and out of proportion to its share of the contrast pairs (a simplicity bias toward the lowest-description-length separating feature), so that a measured gain decomposes into an instrument-compliance term that saturates at low dose and a competence term that is overwritten at high dose -- and can construct-valid gain be defined operationally as the part invariant under perturbation of the verifier environment (re-scoring fixed weights and retained generations under Python 3.14), with no optimization pressure against the verifier at all?
gap.hypothesis: DPO on binary execution verdicts allocates its update first to the cheapest chosen-vs-rejected discriminator; for this corpus that is 'emit from typing import' (a single early-token decision that flips a NameError). Therefore (i) pairs whose rejected half fails ONLY by a typing NameError are a minority (5-30% of the 918; the 13 seed prompts carry no annotations, so the annotations were model-introduced) yet all three retrains learn the import to near-saturation (typing fails 11 -> 2 per 155 generations) and 51-58% of each +10pp is attributable to it: amplification ratio (behavior share / contrast share) >= 2; (ii) along the training trajectory the implicit-reward margin on typing-class pairs saturates before logic-error-class pairs; (iii) the learned behavior is a saturating (step) function of typing-pair dose, not proportional; (iv) removing or neutralizing typing contrasts (against a size-matched random-drop control) removes the typing behavior and leaves the +3 to +6pp residual on the same two tasks (ace_oss_17851, ace_oss_24748), and that residual does not track per-task test weakness; (v) label-swapping reverses it; (vi) amplification is monotone in update magnitude (poscontrol: 0.1 typing fails/row, typing-forgiven gain +2.0pp); (vii) re-scoring the SAME generations under a Python 3.14 verifier removes the typing component and leaves the residual. Consequently the robustness results for stochastic verifier noise (1/(1-2 eps) penalties; tolerance to 15-40% flips) do not transfer to execution verifiers, whose systematic error is anti-robust because it is learnable: the relevant quantity is not the verifier's FP rate but the learnability (contrast consistency, description length) of its error.
gap.why_untouched: verifier-hacking is crowded (4/5) on the adversarial axis, but its OPEN list names this exact sub-question three times: 'Base rate of latent-hole triggering under ZERO optimization pressure: no paper measures how often an unoptimized sampler ... trips a verifier false positive; Ray (2026) fuzzes synthetic defects and Rajan (2026) explicitly declines to decompose accidental vs learned exploitation'; 'Propagation of verifier holes through OFFLINE preference learning: every hacking study uses online RL or agentic inference; whether DPO on execution verdicts amplifies a hole that appears only at the sampler's natural rate is untested'; 'Non-adversarial verdict-channel corruption (... interpreter-version ground-truth drift ...) lies outside every published taxonomy'; plus 'Does a measured training gain survive verifier hardening ... how much of a +10pp effect is inflation vs generalizable improvement, and do per-task gains (F5) correlate with test-suite weakness?' and Rajan's stated open causal test (train on fixed vs untouched broken signal at fixed compute). rlvr-code (4/5) OPEN: 'Harness-level verifier integrity ... interpreter-version-dependent ground truth (F6); verifier-noise theory assumes stationary random noise, not structured environment-conditional flips'. test-adequacy-label-noise (3/5) OPEN: 'Asymmetric, task-correlated noise ... has no DPO theory; rDPO/ROPO assume symmetric random flips and Cai et al. only treat policy gradient'; 'Environment-dependent ground truth (interpreter version ...) as a source of verdict noise is undocumented'; 'No controlled study varies verifier FP rate and measures the effect on offline LoRA-DPO'; 'Whether code-DPO gains depend on label content at all ... has not been tested on Llama3'; 'Verifier-hackability audits and fuzzers (Rajan; Ray) measure verifier defects but never train on the defective signal'. eval-metrology (3/5) OPEN: 'No one treats the verifier/harness (sandbox, sentinel protocol, interpreter version) as part of the instrument requiring calibration'. random-adapter-null (2/5) OPEN: swapped-label preference pairs on llama3-8b under LoRA-DPO untested (the Kung & Peng sham control has no DPO analogue). heterogeneous-effects OPEN: 'Spurious Rewards leaves open whether DPO with shuffled/random preference labels on an execution-verified code corpus yields gains on Llama3'. What exists: 'Before the Model Learns the Bug: Fuzzing RLVR Verifiers' (FP 0.557 for a buggy harness, synthetic defects, no training); 'Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments' (declines to decompose accidental vs learned); 'The Obfuscation Atlas (MBPP-Honeypot)' (same Llama-3-8B family but ONLINE RL against a deliberately hackable verifier); 'Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable yet Noisy Rewards under Imperfect Verifiers' (stationary asymmetric channel, policy gradient only); 'Provably Robust DPO' and 'Impact of Preference Noise' (symmetric flips); 'An Imperfect Verifier is Good Enough' (synthetic symmetric noise, on-policy, 15% tolerance); 'Noisy Data is Destructive to RLVR' (the robustness narrative itself suffers F6-type failures); 'Code-R1' (names execution-environment mismatch without measuring it); 'Do Models Really Learn to Follow Instructions?' (format-learning sham control, instruction tuning only); 'Spurious Rewards' (content-free signals do not move Llama3, making the result informative); AceCoder/PLUM/CodeDPO/Sol-Ver report single-run gains on annotated-signature prompts with no environment counterfactual. Nobody has a naturally occurring, deterministic, environment-conditional verdict quirk that a policy learned under offline DPO at the sampler's natural rate, measured as a corpus-dose -> behavior-amplification curve, decomposed against the same benchmark with a counterfactual verifier. gap.theoretical_payoff: Replaces the stationary-noise picture of imperfect verifiers with a learnability picture: DPO's margin gradient is steepest along the cheapest edit that flips the most rejected halves, so a systematic, environment-conditional failure cause is learned first, amplified far beyond its corpus share and saturated before the construct-relevant signal -- structured, one-sided, learnable verdict 'noise' that neither the stationary-noise RL theory (Cai et al.) nor symmetric-flip DPO theory (rDPO; Gao et al.) describes, and whose relevant quantity is the learnability of the verifier's error, not its FP rate. It is the deflationary dual of reward hacking: the model learns the instrument rather than the task with zero optimization against the verifier, supplying the offline-propagation measurement and the zero-pressure base rate that the verifier-hacking literature (Ray; Rajan; MBPP-Honeypot) leaves open and the first offline-regime answer to Rajan's causal test. It makes the psychometric instrument/construct distinction operational for RLVR: construct-valid gain = gain invariant under verifier-environment perturbation (change the instrument's environment, hold the weights fixed), with the instrument term's share growing with dose (F5c's collapse from +11.4 to +2.0pp) -- a counterfactual re-verification protocol that turns 'instrument integrity' from a taxonomy into a measurable share of any reported gain, and a reporting standard for every code-DPO/RLVR paper whose benchmark prompts carry typing annotations (AceCoder, PLUM, CodeDPO, Sol-Ver). Readers would have to re-examine 'An Imperfect Verifier is Good Enough' (15% tolerance holds for unstructured noise; structured noise is learned, not tolerated), 'Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable yet Noisy Rewards' (the channel is not stationary), 'Spurious Rewards' (Llama3 does not gain from random rewards but does from systematic instrument-correlated rewards -- the gain is signal-driven, the signal is about the verifier), and 'Code-R1' (false positives 'confuse the model'; systematic false negatives teach it). Matters to code-RLVR/DPO authors (what a +10pp on an execution benchmark means), verifier-noise theorists (a structured non-stationary task-correlated noise model), reward-hacking researchers, benchmark metrologists (the harness as a calibrated instrument), and the F6 instrument-integrity taxonomy (interpreter-version ground truth becomes a measured term).

evidence: CLOSEST PRIOR (partial overlap, online-RL regime): 'When the Reward Suite Is Leaky: A Preregistered Causal Contrast of Natural Verifier False Positives in RLVR' (arXiv 2607.11022, Jul 2026, single author Chuyifei Zhang) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11022 . Runs exactly the 'train on broken vs hardened signal at fixed compute' causal test the gap cites as Rajan's open question, on NATURAL (not injected) per-task persistent asymmetric false positives: GRPO on MBPP rewarded by leaky original tests vs hardened MBPP+ tests, preregistered, with a pre-training static leakiness audit (Spearman 0.80 with rewarded FP mass) and a zero-pressure observation ('untrained base models already produce the same wrong outputs under the leaky filter'). Concludes hardening removes measurement inflation, and — crucially — finds NO amplification ('FP incidence does not grow within our horizon'; selection of pre-existing error modes rather than learned exploitation). It is online GRPO only: no DPO/offline arm, no interpreter-version or execution-environment manipulation, no re-scoring of the SAME fixed generations under a swapped verifier environment (verified by direct fetch of the abstract page). This paper removes three items from the gap's 'why_untouched' inventory (natural-FP causal contrast, hardening decomposition of inflation, zero-pressure base rate — all for online RL), but its no-amplification result actually makes the gap's DPO-amplification hypothesis a live, contested question rather than an established one.

'Delay, Plateau, or Collapse: Evaluating the Impact of Systematic Verification Error on RLVR' (arXiv 2605.02909, May 2026, v2 Aug 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02909 . Directly establishes the gap's conceptual punchline for ONLINE RLVR: 'outcomes are not determined by the overall error rate but by the specific pattern of introduced errors' — systematic FPs cause plateaus-to-collapse, unlike random noise. But: injected/synthetic errors, arithmetic tasks, online RL, no environment-conditional error, no gain decomposition, no dose-response amplification measurement. The claim 'structured verifier error is qualitatively different from stochastic flips and FP-rate is not the relevant quantity' is therefore no longer untouched, though its offline-DPO, natural-quirk, learnability-quantified version is.

'Rate or Fate? RLVeR: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Noisy Rewards' (arXiv 2601.04411, Jan 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04411 . Replicator-dynamics bandit theory of RLVR with mode-conditional TPR/FPR (a form of structured noise); predicts a sharp phase transition at Youden's index J=TPR-FPR with incorrect modes AMPLIFYING when J<0; validated on programming tasks with synthetic noise. Online GRPO theory only; no offline DPO, no natural environment-conditional errors, no description-length/learnability quantity, no benchmark-gain decomposition. Partially pre-empts 'no theory for structured noise'.

'Quantifying Empirical Compute-Supervision Tradeoffs in RLVR' (arXiv 2605.25252, May 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25252 . Injects controlled FP/FN noise into GRPO on GSM8K (Qwen2.5); finds noise-induced gaps persist under compute scaling and FNs hurt more than FPs. Online, injected, math; contradicts the 'rate not fate' robustness narrative empirically but does not touch offline DPO or environment-conditional verdicts.

'An Imperfect Verifier is Good Enough: Learning with Noisy Rewards' (arXiv 2604.07666, Apr 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07666 . Confirms the gap's characterization: robustness to ~15% noise, synthetic/stochastic, on-policy — the robustness result the gap aims to show does not transfer to deterministic environment-conditional error. Not a refuter; the contrast target.

'Spurious Correlation Learning in Preference Optimization: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Mitigation via Tie Training' (arXiv 2605.11134, May 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11134 . Unified THEORY that DPO-style objectives induce reliance on spurious features (mean spurious bias + causal-spurious leakage, log-linear policies), with irreducible distribution-shift vulnerability. Establishes at the mechanism level that DPO learns spurious discriminators — but no execution verifiers, no amplification-ratio or dose-response measurement on a natural corpus, no verifier-environment counterfactual, no measured-gain decomposition.

'Disentangling Length from Quality in Direct Preference Optimization' (Park, Rafailov, Ermon, Finn; arXiv 2403.19159, 2024) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19159 . The canonical existing instance of the gap's schema in the chat domain: DPO exploits the cheapest discriminating feature of preference pairs (length), and controlling the instrument for that feature (length-controlled win rates, up to 20% swing) reveals a compliance component of the measured gain. Makes the qualitative claim 'DPO latches onto a cheap discriminator and part of the gain is instrument compliance' unsurprising in general — but it is judge-based chat evaluation, not a deterministic execution-environment verdict, with no corpus-dose census, no saturation-ordering trajectory, and no fixed-weight re-scoring under a swapped verifier environment.

'Is poisoning a real threat to LLM alignment? Maybe more so than you think' (arXiv 2406.12091, 2024) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12091 , plus 'Best-of-Venom' (2404.05530), 'Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF' (2605.02495), 'Policy Teaching via Data Poisoning in Learning from Human Preferences' (2503.10228). Establishes in the ADVERSARIAL-injection regime that a small minority of preference pairs (as low as 0.5% for DPO backdoors vs ~4% for PPO) implants a behavior — i.e., minority-pair-to-saturated-behavior in offline DPO is directionally established, but for deliberately constructed poison, not a naturally occurring verifier regularity, and with no verifier-side counterfactual or gain decomposition.

'School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs' (Taylor, Chua, Betley, Treutlein, Evans; arXiv 2508.17511, Aug 2025) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17511 . Offline (SFT) acquisition of reward-hacking behavior from ~1,000 curated hack demonstrations, including coding tasks — shows verifier-exploiting behavior can be learned from static data, but from deliberate demonstrations, not from execution-labeled preference pairs at the sampler's natural rate, and measures generalization/misalignment, not gain decomposition.

'Building to the Test: Coding Agents Deliver What You Check, Not What You Requested' (arXiv 2606.28430, Jun 2026) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28430 . Construct-validity framing of oracle-driven coding ('construction-validity problems' where agents optimize oracle feedback); inference-time agentic behavior, no training-signal propagation, no environment swap.

verdicts.what_survives: The composite central question is unanswered in the literature: no paper trains OFFLINE DPO on execution verdicts from a verifier whose error is a naturally occurring, DETERMINISTIC, ENVIRONMENT-CONDITIONAL function (interpreter-version-dependent typing NameError) present at the sampler's natural rate, measures the amplification ratio (behavior share of the gain vs the error class's share of contrast pairs) and its dose-response/saturation ordering, and operationally defines construct-valid gain as the component invariant under re-scoring FIXED weights and retained generations in a swapped verifier environment (3.11 vs 3.14). However, the gap's rhetorical framing needs updating in four places: (1) 'Delay, Plateau, or Collapse' (2605.02909) and 'Rate or Fate' (2601.04411) already establish for online RLVR that systematic/structured verifier error behaves qualitatively differently from random noise and that error PATTERN, not rate, determines outcomes — the 'structured noise is untheorized' claim now holds only for the offline-DPO and natural-environment-quirk versions; (2) 'When the Reward Suite Is Leaky' (2607.11022) already executes the preregistered natural-FP leaky-vs-hardened causal contrast, the static pre-training audit, the zero-pressure base-rate observation, and the 'hardening removes measurement inflation' decomposition — for online GRPO with weak test suites; the gap's strongest surviving move is that this paper found SELECTION WITHOUT AMPLIFICATION (FP incidence does not grow), so the gap's predicted amplification ratio >= 2 under offline DPO would be a genuine regime contrast (offline contrastive gradients amplify what online rejection-sampling merely selects), and a null would be equally informative — either way not pre-empted; (3) the qualitative schema 'DPO learns the cheapest discriminator and instrument-controlled evaluation removes that part of the gain' is established by the length-bias line (2403.19159, length-controlled evaluation) and theorized by 2605.11134, and minority-pair implantation is established by preference poisoning (0.5% suffices, 2406.12091) — so the gap's novelty rests on the naturally-occurring, verifier-side, environment-conditional instance with quantified dose-response and per-task attribution, not on the bare existence of shortcut amplification in DPO; (4) interpreter-version-dependent ground truth remains completely undocumented as a measured training-signal phenomenon (multiple searches, zero hits), making that the safest uniquely-novel pillar. evidence: Shah et al., 'The Pitfalls of Simplicity Bias in Neural Networks' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07710): networks rely EXCLUSIVELY on the simplest predictive feature and stay invariant to complex features even when the simple feature is less predictive — the gap's 'lowest-description-length separating feature learned to the exclusion of competence' is this phenomenon relabeled.

Zhao et al., 'Men Also Like Shopping' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.09457): 'bias amplification' is a named, quantified metric — a trained model exhibits a dataset correlation at a higher rate than its corpus share (33% -> 68%); the gap's 'amplification ratio = behavior share / contrast share >= 2' is this metric under another name.

Pezeshki et al., 'Gradient Starvation' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.09468): dynamical-systems account of the fastest-learned feature dominating the trajectory and starving other predictive features — covers the gap's saturation-ordering prediction (ii) qualitatively.

Arpit et al., 'A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05394): consistent simple patterns are learned before inconsistent noise — makes 'deterministic verifier error is learned as signal while stochastic flips are tolerated' a corollary-level statement.

Park et al., 'Disentangling Length from Quality in Direct Preference Optimization' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19159): offline DPO already shown to 'significantly exploit' a simple spurious feature (length) present in preference pairs — the existence proof that offline DPO amplifies a cheap pair-discriminator is not new.

Rafailov et al., 'Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02900): hacking-like overoptimization occurs in offline DAAs with no reward model and no online optimization pressure, often within one epoch — weakens the 'offline regime is untested for hacking-like effects' framing.

Dubois et al., 'Length-Controlled AlpacaEval' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04475): an explicit counterfactual decomposition of a measured preference-eval gain into an instrument-preference component and a quality component ('what would the preference be if lengths were equal') — the gap's decomposition protocol has a direct methodological precedent.

Gardner et al., 'Contrast Sets' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02709) and Gururangan et al., 'Annotation Artifacts in NLI' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02324): artifact-inflated benchmark scores and perturbation-of-the-instrument evaluation to recover the construct-valid part are standard NLP methodology (up to 25% drops on perturbed test sets).

Geirhos et al., 'Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07780) and Lapuschkin et al., 'Unmasking Clever Hans Predictors' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10178): the general taxonomy — high benchmark scores from unintended cues, unmasked by transfer/perturbation tests.

Campbell's law / Koretz audit-test tradition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campbell%27s_law): psychometrics long ago operationalized 'gain that survives an instrument swap' — score inflation on a high-stakes test detected by re-measuring the construct with an audit test; 'construct-valid gain = instrument-perturbation-invariant gain' is this, made operational for a code verifier.

Skalse et al., 'Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13085): the formal reward-hacking definition requires active optimization against the proxy — confirming the gap's zero-pressure regime sits OUTSIDE the reward-hacking formalism (bounds the adjacency; supports the surviving part).

Zhang et al., 'Learning with Feature-Dependent Label Noise' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.07756): label-noise theory already treats structured feature-dependent noise as fundamentally different from i.i.d. class-conditional noise — but as a robustness/correction problem, not as a decomposition of training gains under a shared train/eval instrument.

Gruber et al., 'An Empirical Study of Flaky Tests in Python' (ICST 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.09077): environment-conditional test verdicts are a documented SE phenomenon — 28% of 7,571 Python flaky tests caused by test infrastructure rather than the code under test.

Shuieh et al., 'Assessing Robustness to Spurious Correlations in Post-Training Language Models' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05704): closest 2025 neighbor — injects spurious correlations at varied rates (10%/90%) into SFT/DPO/KTO — but synthetic injection, no code/execution verifier, no amplification-ratio or counterfactual-verifier decomposition reported in the abstract.

2025-2026 arXiv API sweeps ('shortcut learning'+'preference optimization'; 'reward hacking'+'direct preference optimization', sorted by submission date, e.g. https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:%22shortcut%20learning%22%20AND%20all:%22preference%20optimization%22): hits are multimodal-hallucination DPO papers (2605.31312, 2509.24491) and domain-specific reward-hacking mitigations (2608.06526, 2607.10191, 2606.03216) — none train on execution-verdict labels or decompose gains via a counterfactual verifier environment. Caveat: WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this task; searches ran via arXiv API + targeted fetches, and two API queries were rate-limited (HTTP 429).

What survives as genuinely open is the narrower quantitative sub-question no adjacent field touches: for a NATURALLY OCCURRING, deterministic, interpreter-version-conditional execution-verdict error (not injected, not adversarial, at the sampler's natural rate) used as offline DPO labels for code, (a) the measured propagation curve — amplification ratio, dose step-function, and margin-trajectory ordering by rejected-error class; (b) the dual-interpreter (3.11 vs 3.14) re-scoring of fixed weights and retained generations as a decomposition of a reported +10pp into instrument-compliance vs residual on the SAME benchmark; and (c) the theory claim that verifier-noise robustness results (symmetric-flip 1/(1-2eps) bounds, 15-40% tolerance) are governed by the wrong parameter — the learnability/contrast-consistency of the verifier's error, not its FP rate — which no verifier-noise, label-noise, or reward-hacking formalism states (Skalse's definition explicitly requires optimization pressure, so the zero-pressure regime is outside it; Rafailov's DAA overoptimization is KL-budget degradation, not learned instrument error). gap.title: Block-scale capture: blockwise 8-bit Adam stops being Adam in the 256-element quantization block that holds Llama-3-8B's massive-activation channel, and an Adam-displacement invariant detects it without a replica
gap.central_question: Are the ~170 elements of layers.1.mlp.down_proj.lora_A that exceed the exact-Adam worst-case displacement bound (3.16 x sum(lr) = 0.0547) by up to 3x -- all inside the 256-aligned column window [2304,2559], which contains intermediate channel 2427 that Probe 4 measured as a prompt-invariant massive activation (max|x| 386.5 vs median 0.013, 30,000x), while lora_A everywhere else stays inside its kaiming init box -- produced by bitsandbytes' blockwise (blocksize 256) 8-bit quantization of Adam's second-moment state being dominated by that one channel, so that the recorded optimizer ('adamw_bnb_8bit') silently applies a non-Adam update rule to the channel's 255 block-neighbours in every run on this model; is the effect deterministic and model-conditioned rather than data- or seed-conditioned; is it functionally material; and can the per-tensor bound |delta theta| <= 3.16 x sum(lr_t) -- which holds for exact Adam regardless of seed, data order or kernel nondeterminism -- serve as a free, replica-free training-time integrity invariant that separates optimizer artifacts from benign nondeterminism and from hardware faults (F4)?
gap.hypothesis: dL/dA[:, j] scales with the input activation x_j, so channel 2427's 30,000x activation makes its gradient second moment set the 256-element block's absmax; the 255 neighbours' v underflow in the 8-bit dynamic format, their effective step sizes explode past the Adam bound, while 2427's own entries (the absmax holder) stay accurate -- exactly Probe 4's signature (column 2427 itself NOT an outlier at 0.0044; neighbours up to 0.175, 21x the init bound; 93 columns x all 16 rank rows). With identical seed and data order the excess vanishes under 32-bit optimizer states (adamw_torch, or adamw_bnb_8bit with min_8bit_size raised above the 229,376-element tensor) and reappears under adamw_bnb_8bit and paged_adamw_8bit, localized to the same block regardless of seed or corpus; it recurs at every learning rate relative to sum(lr); and it is either functionally measurable or demonstrably immaterial (Probe 4 predicts immaterial for this adapter: the block holds 70.4% of layer-1 down_proj's ||dW||_F^2 but 0.94% of the whole adapter's, and the layer's activation-weighted output delta is ~entirely channel 2427's contribution because the neighbours' activations are ~0.013) -- in both cases 'adamw_bnb_8bit' is a well-formed recorded config value that does not describe the applied update (the candidate 7th F6 measurement-integrity failure), and the displacement bound plus a step-1 A-invariance check is a closed-form post-hoc detector needing no replica, no determinism and no recomputation.
gap.why_untouched: No angle in the 12-angle map covers optimizer-state quantization, and no paper known to the map reports an interaction between massive activations / super weights and blockwise optimizer-state quantization; the nearest angles are the least crowded. silent-hardware-faults (2/5) OPEN: 'Cheap detection without a replica: Ma et al. recommend a shadow data-parallel replica ...; Altenbernd's detector needs seeded recomputation; SDCHunter needs replay. Nothing addresses a single consumer GPU with no second device, no ECC, and an unseeded training script'; 'Fine-tuning regime is unstudied: arXiv returns zero results for silent data corruption + fine-tuning and for LoRA + silent data corruption'; 'Fault models for controlled experiments remain contested ... corruption is address-periodic' (Tung et al.) -- F10 is exactly an address-periodic (256-aligned), model-conditioned, deterministic corruption, but of SOFTWARE origin, a class no SDC paper considers; 'Attestation of effect rather than structure' is unaddressed (Shang et al.'s drift proofs certify that dW is low-rank, not that it came from the declared update rule). null-results-prereg-norms (2/5) ESTABLISHED cites the Oct 2024 silent gradient-accumulation bug in this very transformers/TRL stack and 'Silent Bugs in Deep Learning Frameworks' as the definitional category; its OPEN list asks for 'a taxonomy ... plus adapter-level forensic signatures' of silent instrument failure in small-scale post-training and names recorded-vs-effective config mismatch. seed-variance-reproducibility (2/5): the TRL unseeded-init audit is the same genre (a library default that does not do what the record says; training_args.bin records seed=42, gradient_checkpointing=False, warmup_steps=0 and optim=adamw_bnb_8bit, none of which describe the run). random-adapter-null / rlvr-code: 'The Path Not Taken' documents a bf16 'precision gate' that HIDES micro-updates -- the complement, 8-bit state quantization INFLATING updates in outlier blocks, is unreported; lora-solution-geometry's 'LoRA Training Provably Converges ... or It Fails Loudly' describes only loud large-magnitude failures, and Hayou et al.'s lazy A makes any A displacement beyond sum(lr) anomalous, which is what makes the detector cheap; 'LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence' and every intruder-dimension / norm / geometry analysis of QLoRA adapters would be silently contaminated by this block. What exists: SDC detectors that require a replica, seeded recompute or replay ('Understanding Silent Data Corruption in LLM Training'; 'Exploring Silent Data Corruption as a Reliability Challenge in LLM Training', whose update-magnitude detector is the closest cousin of the Adam-bound check; 'Training with Confidence (TrainCheck)' invariants never derived from the optimizer's update rule); the super-weight and massive-activation papers characterize the coordinates but never their interaction with quantized optimizer state (outside the map; Probe 4 verified that Yu et al. 2024, arXiv 2411.07191, does NOT list Llama-3-8B -- the [788,2427] coordinate is supported by this machine's measurement, not by that citation). Nobody has reported that 8-bit blockwise Adam produces localized non-Adam steps around massive-activation columns, nor a post-hoc detector for it. The project's head start: F10/Probe 4 is the only observed instance -- the bound is derived (fp32 master weights, weight_decay 0, sum lr 0.0173), the scan of all 224 A tensors is done (exactly one tensor, one block), the base-model activation hook is done (channel 2427, inside the block; layers 0 and 2 have no comparable channel), the materiality is computed, the adapter, training_args.bin, the cached 4-bit base, a working venv and a 25-minute ablation are all in hand.
predictions: Zero-compute full scan (anchor, largely confirmed by Probe 4): the only tensors violating (init box + 3.16*sum(lr)) are layers.1.mlp.down_proj.lora_A (169-170 elements in [2304,2559], all 16 rank rows, 93 columns; mean max|A| per column 0.058 inside vs 0.009 outside) plus one stray element in layers.31.mlp.up_proj.lora_B; the block carries >= 25% of that layer's ||dW||_F^2 (measured 70.4%, vs 1.8% if uniform) but < 5% of the whole adapter's (measured 0.94%); no other 256-block in any of the 224 A tensors has more than 5 elements beyond bound+worst-case. REFUTED if violations are scattered across layers/blocks -- would point to clipping, TDR or kernel faults, not state quantization.

Gradient witness: a 1-step hook on layer-1 down_proj lora_A.grad shows channel 2427's grad^2 exceeds its block-mates' median by >= 100x, and the in-block vs out-of-block ratio of mean |A| displacement tracks that channel's gradient-energy ratio; channel 198's block [0,255] (next-largest activation, 46.3; within-block dynamic range ~70x smaller) shows a weaker version or none. REFUTED if the gradient ratio is < 10x or the massive channel's block shows no excess on rerun.

Emulation: numpy Adam with 256-block absmax-quantized second moments (bnb dynamic map) fed gradient columns with one channel ~100x the others reproduces neighbour steps >= 2-3x the worst-case bound while exact fp32 Adam reproduces none; the emulator discriminates v-underflow from first-moment, minimum-representable-value and gradient-clipping explanations.

Fixed-seed ablation (--max-steps 20, lr 2e-4, seeded A0 so A_trained - A_init is exact): adamw_bnb_8bit reproduces >= 50-100 elements beyond 1/sqrt(fan_in) + 3.16*sum(lr), all in [2304,2559] of layer-1 down_proj (deterministic location); adamw_torch shows 0 such elements in all 448 tensors; paged_adamw_8bit matches bnb_8bit; adamw_bnb_8bit with min_8bit_size raised above the tensor sizes shows 0. REFUTED if adamw_torch also exceeds the bound (gradient clipping, a kernel fault or TDR is the cause), if the excess depends on paging rather than bit width, if bnb's excess is not block-aligned on rerun (a non-reproducible event, which would reopen F4), or if it lands in a different window at a different seed or corpus (not column-conditioned).

Dose-independence: at the original recipe (lr 5e-6, sum(lr) ~1.6e-4) the same block exceeds 3.16*sum(lr) ~5e-4 in exact displacement A_T - A_0 while remaining inside the kaiming box -- the artifact is relative to the bound, not to the init scale, and functionally <= ~5% of A's element scale, so the three retrains' functional identity is unaffected; at lr 2e-4 x 3 epochs the block carries > 5% of that layer's ||dW||_F (measured 70%). REFUTED if the low-lr block shows no excess relative to its bound or the share is < 1%.

Functional materiality (measured, not assumed): seeded 8-bit vs 32-bit 1-epoch adapters scored interleaved: immaterial if raw per-task r >= 0.85 (at the reliability ceiling) and |delta gain| <= 3pp; material if r < 0.7 or |delta gain| > 5pp; a block-clipped copy of dpo_adapter_poscontrol (A in the window clipped to the init bound) shifts the profile in the same direction as the 32-bit adapter or sits within +/-3pp of intact. Probe 4 predicts 'immaterial'; the 'material' sub-hypothesis is refuted by r >= 0.95 -- still the point: the invariant detects a process failure the benchmark cannot see, and the side observation stands that the layer-1 down_proj LoRA acts as a learned prompt-invariant constant offset B*A[:,2427]*386 in the residual stream.

Gate: the step-1 invariant (every lora_B nonzero, every lora_A bitwise unchanged because dL/dA = 0 when B = 0) and the end-of-run invariant (max|B| <= 3.16*sum(lr) per tensor; max|A - A0| <= 3.16*sum(lr)) pass on adamw_torch runs, and the A-bound fails only on the layer-1 block under bnb; the pair separates 'dead update' from 'non-Adam update'.

Public-adapter scan: Llama-3-8B QLoRA adapters on the HF hub that target down_proj and were trained with 8-bit/paged optimizers show the same block signature in layers.1.mlp.down_proj.lora_A in the majority of cases; adapters trained with 32-bit states do not. REFUTED if the signature is absent in most 8-bit-trained adapters.

gap.theoretical_payoff: Establishes a new, deterministic, silent update-corruption class: blockwise-quantized optimizer states break Adam's per-coordinate invariance wherever a block contains an outlier coordinate, and LLMs with massive activations / super weights guarantee such outliers at fixed, model-conditioned addresses -- so every 8-bit-Adam LoRA run on these models applies a non-Adam update rule to ~255 neighbours of the massive-activation channel while recording 'adamw_bnb_8bit'. Unlike hardware SDC it is reproducible, address-periodic by software construction, and model-conditioned, which adds a software corruption class to the F6 taxonomy of components that emit well-formed numbers after they stop doing what the record says (the 7th measurement-integrity failure). It gives fine-tuning its first optimizer-derived integrity invariant: exact Adam bounds per-coordinate displacement by 3.16*sum(lr) independently of seed, data order or kernel nondeterminism, so the bound plus step-1 A-invariance is the replica-free, determinism-free, recomputation-free detector that the SDC literature says does not exist for a single consumer GPU -- an attestation of EFFECT rather than structure, usable as a two-line gate in any PEFT pipeline, and one that flags a process failure the benchmark cannot see. Mechanistically it shows block-wise state quantization fails exactly where the model is most sensitive (the premise that outliers are confined to their block holds, but inside that block the neighbours receive non-Adam steps), and that any weight-space geometry, norm or intruder-dimension analysis of QLoRA adapters trained with 8-bit Adam on such models is contaminated in a known window. Readers would have to re-examine the QLoRA-era default of 8-bit/paged optimizers for LoRA parameters (the state saving is nil for ~42M parameters; the cost is a silent non-Adam update), the block-wise 8-bit optimizer paper's equivalence claim in the presence of massive activations, 'The Path Not Taken' (bf16 hides micro-updates; quantized states manufacture macro-updates -- a second precision pathology), Altenbernd-style max-RMS detectors (which would mislabel this as hardware SDC), and the project's own F4 TDR hypothesis. Matters to every QLoRA / unsloth / axolotl user on Llama-family models, bitsandbytes maintainers and optimizer designers (block size vs outlier channels), and the training-integrity / attestation community.

evidence: Kingma & Ba, 'Adam' (ICLR 2015), Sec 2.1, verbatim from PDF: 'The effective stepsize has two upper bounds: |Delta_t| <= alpha*(1-beta1)/sqrt(1-beta2) in the case (1-beta1) > sqrt(1-beta2), and |Delta_t| <= alpha otherwise ... This can be understood as establishing a trust region.' With defaults this is exactly 3.16*alpha, so the gap's per-tensor displacement bound 3.16*sum(lr_t) is a one-line corollary of the original Adam paper, not a new invariant. https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6980

Li, Chen & Zhu, 'Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States' (NeurIPS 2023): identifies the 'zero point problem of quantizing the second moment' -- 'small quantization error of values around zero will cause catastrophically large deviation of the update direction' -- and shows 'moments have complicated outlier patterns, that current block-wise quantization cannot accurately approximate,' with outliers persisting in fixed rows/columns. This is the gap's core mechanism (v under-resolution in outlier-dominated blocks -> inflated steps), published for optimizer states in 2023, though framed as a 4-bit problem with 8-bit treated as the working baseline. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01507

Shazeer & Stern, 'Adafactor' (2018): 'adaptive methods can produce larger-than-desired updates when the decay rate of the second moment accumulator is too slow. We propose update clipping.' The phenomenon family (underestimated v -> oversized updates) is textbook, with a standard remedy. https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04235

Wortsman, Dettmers et al., 'Stable and low-precision training for large-scale vision-language models' (2023): loss spikes 'consistently occur 1-8 iterations after the squared gradients become under-estimated by their AdamW second moment estimator' (StableAdamW/AdamW-Adafactor hybrid). Same family: v-underestimation inflating steps, from staleness rather than blockwise quantization. https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13013

Dettmers et al., '8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization' (2021): blockwise + dynamic quantization explicitly motivated by precision 'for both large and small magnitude values' and stability; claims accuracy parity with 32-bit. No report of localized, model-conditioned artifacts near outlier channels -- the gap's finding would be a direct counterexample to this paper's equivalence claim. https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02861

Yu et al., 'The Super Weight in Large Language Models' (arXiv 2411.07191): Table 2 super-weight directory covers Llama 7B/13B/30B, Llama2 7B/13B, Mistral-7B, OLMo, Phi-3 -- Llama-3-8B is NOT listed and coordinate [788,2427] does not appear; scope is inference-time weight/activation quantization only, no optimizer states. verdicts.what_survives: Two of the gap's three pillars are relabelings and should not be claimed as new: (1) the displacement bound 3.16*sum(lr) is a verbatim corollary of Kingma & Ba Sec 2.1 (the trust-region property), and (2) the qualitative mechanism -- blockwise absmax quantization under-resolving small second moments in an outlier-dominated block, with too-small v producing 'catastrophically large' updates -- is documented for optimizer states by Li/Chen/Zhu 2023 (zero-point problem, moment outlier patterns blockwise quantization cannot approximate) and, for the v-underestimation family generally, by Adafactor's update clipping and StableAdamW. A reviewer fluent in that literature would call prediction 3 (the numpy emulation) a reproduction of known physics, and the 'stops being Adam' framing is definitionally weak since adamw_bnb_8bit is recorded as an approximation. What genuinely survives, unclaimed anywhere I could find: (a) the empirical existence proof that PRODUCTION 8-bit blockwise Adam (bnb dynamic map, blocksize 256) violates the Adam trust-region bound by up to 3x in a real QLoRA run -- a counterexample to Dettmers et al.'s accuracy-parity claim and to the 4-bit paper's framing of 8-bit as safe; (b) the coupling of the massive-activation/super-weight literature to optimizer-state quantization: that these models GUARANTEE an outlier gradient coordinate at a fixed, model-conditioned address, making the artifact deterministic and address-periodic (a software corruption class no SDC paper considers; the super-weight follow-up 2607.08733 and the training-dynamics paper 2508.03616 both stop short of optimizer states, and the one recent quantized-state analysis 2603.16731 reports the opposite pathology, staleness); (c) using the known bound as a REPLICA-FREE, recomputation-free post-hoc integrity invariant for fine-tuning (TrainCheck infers invariants from traces, the SDC update-magnitude detector needs recomputation, proof-of-learning needs re-execution) -- the novelty there is not the bound but the demonstration that lazy-A LoRA keeps benign runs far inside it, giving usable separation. The narrower still-open question: 'Does production 8-bit blockwise Adam deterministically violate the Adam displacement bound in the quantization block containing a massive-activation channel, and does the closed-form bound give a practically tight replica-free detector for this and other non-Adam updates?' -- with the mechanism section rewritten to cite Li et al. 2023 and Adafactor as known antecedents rather than claiming the underflow-inflation mechanism as new.
