gap.title: What 'the update took' means under nondeterminism: a functional acceptance class calibrated on healthy seeds, a norm-matched random-adapter null, and a fault-type taxonomy separable in function space
gap.central_question: Given that the legitimate outcomes of an unseeded LoRA-DPO procedure are weight-orthogonal adapters with one function (F5b), is 'the update took' definable only as membership in that functional outcome class -- and do corruption phenotypes separate in function space by fault type: omission faults (lost steps) producing a scaled-down copy of the legitimate function, commission faults (wrong gradient values: partial GEMM, kernel abort with resubmission, the 8-bit optimizer-block anomaly) producing an uncorrelated direction at preserved norm -- such that the original F1 'null' adapter (same norm, zero mean, profile uncorrelated with the healthy class at r = -0.10, split-half reliability 0.21/0.52) is classifiable as commission/random and indistinguishable from a norm-matched random LoRA, and such that a single cheap observation of a new adapter (no replica, no seed, no generation) can accept or reject it?
gap.hypothesis: In the lazy LoRA regime the procedure's legitimate outcome class is a single function sampled with instrument noise, so a replica-free, seed-free acceptance test exists: the function-space fingerprint (per-position logit-delta direction on a fixed probe set, or the per-task delta profile) of a healthy run lies within the between-seed dispersion of healthy retrains, while (a) a norm-matched random LoRA (kaiming A, Gaussian B with per-layer ||B||_F or ||B A0||_F matched to a healthy adapter, built on the healthy adapter's own A0), (b) a commission-fault run, and (c) the F1 adapter fall outside it with |cos| < 0.2 and a zero-mean per-task redistribution of low reliability that nonetheless passes an effect-variation test (so F5's permutation criterion alone cannot distinguish trained-null from noise); omission-fault runs stay inside it (cos > 0.8) with proportionally reduced gain; structural integrity checks (per-layer norm, rank, Adam bound) pass for random and commission arms alike and therefore cannot make these distinctions.
gap.why_untouched: silent-hardware-faults (2/5) OPEN: 'Cheap detection without a replica ... Nothing addresses a single consumer GPU with no second device, no ECC, and an unseeded training script'; 'Determinism vs detectability: every replay/recompute/bitwise-alignment oracle assumes a deterministic reference trajectory ... [no paper] proposes a functional (behavioral) oracle for that case'; 'Distinguishing a corrupted optimum from a different-but-healthy optimum: ... no work gives a test that separates the two post hoc from the weights or from evaluation profiles'; 'a kernel-abort (partial GEMM) fault model has not been injected or characterized'; 'Attestation of effect rather than structure: ... nothing certifies that a low-rank dW is in the equivalence class of legitimate outcomes'. random-adapter-null (2/5) OPEN: 'No paper found that uses a norm-matched random LoRA adapter ... as the null arm for a fine-tuning improved the model claim' (Ilharco's random-vector control was for negation on ViT/GPT-2); 'No paper shows a trained-but-ineffective adapter is behaviorally indistinguishable (per-task profile, pass@k, entropy) from a random adapter of the same norm; nor whether it is distinguishable'; 'Whether precision/TDR-style silent update corruption produces adapters that look like random noise, like a scaled-down trained adapter, or like something else'; 'Whether zero-aggregate redistribution (F5) is sharpening (entropy collapse, pass@k bounded), random churn, or partial learning'. heterogeneous-effects (3/5) OPEN: 'No paper defines a null distribution for a noise-like adapter ... The three-way contrast no-op vs random-perturbation vs trained-zero-mean has not been run for any post-training method'; 'Treatment-effect-variation tests (Ding et al.; Crump et al.) and PERMANOVA have never been applied to LLM benchmark matrices with replicates per item'. seed-variance-reproducibility (2/5) OPEN: 'F5's p<5e-5 needs a nondeterminism-only control'. What changed: before F5b the literature had no calibrated legitimate class (Jordan/Zhuang/Summers-Dinneen predict churn from any reseed), so F5's redistribution could not be classified; F5b supplies three healthy retrains at the reliability ceiling and F5 now shows the original adapter at r = -0.10 against them, which makes classification possible for the first time. Missing: the random null arm, controlled omission vs commission fault injection, the function-space statistic, the effect-variation tests, and the optimizer ablation for the F10 block anomaly (an actual non-Adam update found in the one adapter on this machine -- shared with Gap 3). The existing detectors (Ma et al. shadow replica; Altenbernd seeded recompute; SDCHunter replay; OpGuard bitwise alignment; Shang et al. and VeriLoRA structural/cryptographic attestation) all presuppose a deterministic reference update, which F3 shows TRL/PEFT-as-shipped cannot provide.
predictions: Zero-compute classification from existing rows: the original adapter's profile distance to the healthy-class centroid (rep1/2/3) exceeds the within-class distances with replicate-bootstrap p < 0.01 on both 4090 sessions (forged-rep vs null-rep; ctl-his vs ctl-null), while its own cross-session r = 0.47 shows a weakly persistent direction -- the predicted commission/random phenotype, not a scaled-down healthy one; a Ding-Feller-Miratrix effect-variation test (tasks as units, replicates as repeated draws) rejects constant effect for the original adapter vs null at p < 0.01 and PERMANOVA separates {rep1, rep2, rep3} from {original} from {poscontrol}. REFUTED if the original adapter sits within the healthy class once instrument noise is accounted for.

Norm-matched random LoRA (kaiming A or the healthy adapter's own A0, Gaussian B with per-layer norm matched to a healthy seed adapter; plus a 0.5x-scaled variant): aggregate gain within +/-2pp of null; per-task profile vs null passes the effect-variation test at p < 0.01 yet has split-half reliability 0.2-0.5 and |r| < 0.2 with the healthy profile -- reproducing F5's original-adapter signature (reliability 0.21/0.52, r = -0.10) and showing a random adapter is 'not a no-op' by F5's permutation criterion. REFUTED if the random adapter's profile is reliable and correlated with the healthy one (r > 0.5; Neural-Thickets regime: random directions share the task direction), or if its effect variance is indistinguishable from null-vs-null.

Omission arm (50% of optimizer steps' LoRA gradients zeroed on a seeded schedule): function-space cosine with the healthy same-seed adapter >= 0.8, profile r >= 0.8, gain 40-70% of healthy. REFUTED if cosine < 0.3.

Commission arm (20% of steps with within-tensor permuted gradient entries, norm preserved): ||dW||_F within 20% of healthy, function cosine <= 0.3, gain <= +3pp, profile reliability < 0.6. REFUTED if gain >= 70% of healthy (DPO-LoRA is then robust to gross gradient corruption and F1 needs another cause).

Acceptance statistic: the 31-prompt logit-delta fingerprint cosine separates {healthy seeds} from {random, commission} by >= 0.3 with no overlap across >= 3 healthy seeds, at < 10 min per adapter with no generation; structural checks (per-layer norm, rank, Adam bound, intruder-dimension count) pass for random and commission arms alike. REFUTED if healthy-vs-healthy cosines overlap corrupted-vs-healthy.

Optimizer ablation shared with Gap 3 (adamw_torch vs adamw_bnb_8bit, same seed): the [2304,2559] excess in layers.1.mlp.down_proj.lora_A vanishes under 32-bit Adam while the function cosine between the two adapters is >= 0.9 (the F10 anomaly is a real non-Adam update that is functionally immaterial -- a structural flag the functional oracle correctly ignores). REFUTED if function cosine < 0.5 (the block is material).

Mechanism signature (zero-compute from existing draws): pass@k (k <= 5 per replicate, pooled) for base, original adapter, retrains and poscontrol -- the healthy retrains show sharpening (pass@1 up, pass@5 gain smaller), the original adapter shows neither sharpening nor widening (random churn), the random arm matches the original. gap.theoretical_payoff: Would establish that for a nondeterministic training procedure the only coherent notion of 'the update took' is membership in its functional outcome class -- which in the lazy LoRA regime is a single function -- and that corruption phenotypes are separable in function space by fault type (omission -> scaled-down copy; commission -> uncorrelated direction at preserved norm, indistinguishable from a norm-matched random adapter). It reframes Hochlehnert-style replication failures: a null can be a corrupted instrument rather than evaluation variance, and F1 is classified without invoking TDR. Matters to training-integrity and attestation researchers, reproducibility methodologists, consumer-GPU practitioners with no ECC or replica, and the heterogeneous-effects statistics line.

evidence: ADJACENCY HIT (framing): Baker et al., 'A new ensemble-based consistency test for the Community Earth System Model (pyCECT)', GMD 2015 — https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/8/2829/2015/ — accepts a new non-bitwise-reproducible simulation run iff it is statistically indistinguishable from an ensemble of trusted runs; 'has proven its utility in detecting errors in software and hardware environments'. The gap's core concept — a functional acceptance class calibrated on healthy replicates, replacing a deterministic reference — is a decade-old verification paradigm in computational science, contradicting the why_untouched claim that no one 'proposes a functional (behavioral) oracle' for nondeterministic computation. It has, however, never been applied to ML training.

HECT: High-Dimensional Ensemble Consistency Testing for Climate Models — https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04051 — the ECT line is active (classifier-based goodness-of-fit acceptance of runs), still climate-only.

ADJACENCY HIT (mechanism): FLTrust — https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13995 — scores each incoming update by cosine similarity of its DIRECTION to a trusted reference update computed on a clean root dataset, with magnitude normalization; prior art for accept/reject-by-direction-vs-healthy-reference of a training update. Differences: federated multi-client, per-round, weight space not function space, requires the server to compute its own reference update (a replica in effect).

Krum (Blanchard et al.) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02757 — a single worker sending arbitrary/random gradients breaks any linear-combination update rule; defense selects updates by distance to peers. Establishes random-direction corrupted updates and distance-based rejection as a known phenomenon, but requires multiple simultaneous workers.

COROLLARY (prediction 3, omission): Chizat, Oyallon, Bach, 'On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming' — https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07956 — lazy regime = linearized model around init, so dropping steps moves along the same functional direction with smaller magnitude; plus Alistarh et al., 'The Convergence of Sparsified Gradient Methods' — https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.10505 — heavy gradient omission still converges along the task direction. Omission -> scaled-down-same-function is an expected corollary, not a potential discovery.

COROLLARY (prediction 4, commission): concentration of measure / the gap's own F3 arithmetic (E[cos] ~ 1/sqrt(r*fan_in)) makes 'norm-preserving random corruption -> |cos| ~ 0 vs healthy' near-definitional; the informative part is only whether REAL fault models (partial GEMM, resubmission, 8-bit block anomaly) land in that class. Caveat from 'A Little Is Enough' — https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06156 — norm-bounded corruptions can evade direction/statistical detection, so the commission phenotype is not guaranteed detectable in general.

verdicts.what_survives: The gap survives but must be reframed and narrowed. Two of its load-bearing framings are refuted by adjacent fields: (1) the claim that no functional/behavioral oracle for nondeterministic computation exists is false — ensemble consistency testing (CESM-ECT/pyCECT, Baker et al. 2015; HECT 2020) is exactly acceptance-by-membership-in-a-healthy-ensemble-distribution without bitwise reproducibility, and is routinely used to catch software/hardware errors in climate codes; the honest claim is 'no such oracle exists for ML training runs', and the contribution should be framed as porting ensemble-consistency acceptance into function space for unseeded LoRA post-training. (2) The two fault phenotypes are corollaries, not candidate discoveries: omission -> scaled-down-same-function follows from lazy-regime linearity plus SGD-with-dropped-updates theory, and commission -> uncorrelated-at-preserved-norm follows from concentration of measure; FLTrust already accepts updates by cosine-to-trusted-reference with norm normalization, and Byzantine work (Krum, A Little Is Enough) already catalogs random/scaled corrupted updates and direction-based rejection — in weight space, per-round, with replicas. Also, the F10 blockwise-underflow mechanism is documented in Dettmers et al. 2021; only its super-weight-aligned manifestation is new. What is genuinely new and untouched by any field searched: (a) a replica-free, post hoc, function-space acceptance test for a SINGLE adapter from an unseeded consumer-GPU run, calibrated on healthy retrain dispersion (ECT needs the trusted ensemble too, but has never been applied to training artifacts, has no fault taxonomy, and works on simulation output fields); (b) the norm-matched random-LoRA null arm for a 'fine-tuning improved the model' claim (no arXiv precedent; filter-normalized random directions were never used this way); (c) empirical separability of omission vs commission phenotypes for realistic fault models (partial GEMM, kernel-abort resubmission, 8-bit optimizer block anomaly) at LoRA-DPO scale and eval noise — theory predicts the phenotypes but not their separability under a 31-task instrument with reliability 0.2-0.9; (d) effect-variation tests (Ding-Feller-Miratrix, Crump) and PERMANOVA on LLM benchmark replicate matrices, and the specific demonstration that permutation/effect-variation criteria cannot distinguish a trained-null adapter from norm-matched noise while reliability/correlation criteria can; (e) the classification of the original F1 adapter against the F5b-calibrated healthy class. The predictions most at risk of being 'confirmations of the expected' are 3 and 4; the paper's novelty budget should rest on (a)-(e), not on the taxonomy itself.
